channel.title: Redis on DAWN's Blog
channel.description: Recent content in Redis on DAWN's Blog

item.title: Redis Distributed Practice (Part 4): Cluster Architecture, Online Resharding, and Python Client Development
item.description: Part 4 of the Redis Distributed Practice series: In-depth analysis of the Redis Cluster 16384 hash slots sharding mechanism and decentralized Gossip protocol, hands-on deployment of a 7000~7005 six-node distributed cluster, live horizontal scaling with 800 slots resharding, graceful node decommissioning, and Python client integration with standalone instances, Sentinel read/write splitting, and Redis Cluster with compatibility pitfall solutions.

item.title: Redis High Availability Practice (Part 3): Master-Replica Replication and Sentinel Automatic Failover
item.description: Part 3 of the Redis High Availability Practice series: In-depth analysis of the Redis Master-Replica replication mechanism (full BGSAVE synchronization, continuous command propagation, and repl_backlog circular buffer incremental resume), critical warnings against slave data wipeout accidents caused by unpersisted masters, hands-on deployment of a 6380/6381/6382 three-instance replication topology on a single host, and implementation of Sentinel clusters for sub-second subjective/objective down detection, Leader election, and automated failover.

item.title: Redis Core Practice (Part 2): Five Core Data Types, MySQL Hot Cache, and Transaction Features
item.description: Part 2 of the Redis Core Practice series: In-depth analysis of global key lifecycle management (keys/scan/expire/ttl), hands-on practice with Strings, Hash, List, Set, and SortedSet data structures, real-world implementations including high-concurrency counters, WeChat comment streams, friend topology, and TopN leaderboards, importing MySQL 3308 multi-instance hot rows into Redis Hash via Linux pipes, and in-depth comparison between MySQL ACID transactions and Redis weak transactions with WATCH optimistic locking.

item.title: Redis Core Practice (Part 1): Service Deployment, Security Hardening, and Persistence Mechanisms
item.description: Part 1 of the Redis Core Practice series: Systematically reviews Redis cache service positioning and comprehensive comparison with Memcached/Tair, provides step-by-step guidance on source compilation and installation, environment variables, and multi-instance planning under Linux, deeply analyzes the protected-mode mechanism and bind/requirepass security hardening, and details the underlying principles and trade-offs of RDB snapshots and AOF append logs.
